subject: filtering and moving between Cytoscape and rCytoscape (BIG PROBLEMS!)

messages.author: 6b7cfafa8ea1f9eb
messages.subject: filtering and moving between Cytoscape and rCytoscape (BIG PROBLEMS!)
parts:
Hi all,

Here's my problem: I need to be able use rCytoscape to access a
network that has been created in Cytoscape. Specifically, I need to
use rCytoscape to iteratively filter and select edges back in
Cytoscape, based on edge attributes. (ultimately i need to be able to
turn a bunch of nodes and edges on and off in order to do some
animation -- and doing this manually via Cytoscape's internal filters
is simply not a practical option).

I'm banging my head against the wall at this point because apparently
you can't import graphs into rCytoscape from Cytoscape (you can go the
other way easily enough -- that's the main point of rCytoscape). You
can port a graph you create in rCytoscape to Cytoscape; you can
subsequently select nodes or edges in that graph in rCytoscape, and
then filter your Cytoscape network based on that selection; but as far
as I can tell, you can't take a pre-existing network that's in
Cytoscape, import edge attributes into rCytoscape, then select edges
based on some criteria, in order to ultimately move back to Cytoscape
to filter your data.

One solution I thought of was to simply output my network from
Cytoscape to a format that I could open in R (absent rCytoscape), but
this is a dead end too, as R (via the igraph package) can only import
GML, not XGMML, which means I can't get my edge attributes into R.

I should say, I've also got an original excel file that contains all
of my nodes, edges, and node and edge attributes. Might there be a
way I could use this to easily get all this data into R -- all in
order to eventually get my network back into Cytoscape?

Hope this makes sense -- I'm surprised I was able to articulate it at
all, because it's so convoluted!

Any help is greatly greatly greatly appreciated.


Cheers,

Ben

messages.subject: Re: filtering and moving between Cytoscape and rCytoscape (BIG PROBLEMS!)
parts:
Hi Ben,

Have you tried to command "existing.CytoscapeWindow"? If desired, this
copies the network graph back to R. I'm not sure how it copies the
attributes, as I use it to re-join a saved graph in R with an existing
Cytoscape network, but with some tweaking it might work.

Cheers,

-Robert

messages.author: 195a5e75ebedb149
messages.subject: Re: filtering and moving between Cytoscape and rCytoscape (BIG PROBLEMS!)
parts:
Robert's suggestion should work, existing.CytoscapeWindow works for me.  

You could always start from the spreadsheet file.  Here is how I plot from a tab-delmited .txt file (saved from a spreadsheet and imported into R).  Two functions
 plot.cy <-function (cytoscape.file) {
mydata <- new("graphNEL", edgemode='undirected', nodes=as.character(cytoscape.file[, 1]))
# Set up and load all the node attributes
for (i in 2:ncol(cytoscape.file)) {
mydata <- initNodeAttribute (graph=mydata,  attribute.name=names(cytoscape.file[i]), attribute.type='numeric', default.value=0.0)
nodeData (mydata, n=as.character(cytoscape.file[, 1]), attr=names(cytoscape.file[i])) <- as.numeric(cytoscape.file[,i])
}
# load standard edge attributes
mydata <- initEdgeAttribute (graph= mydata, attribute.name='edgeType', attribute.type='char', default.value='undefined')
  mydata <- initEdgeAttribute(mydata, attribute.name = "Weight", attribute.type = "numeric", default.value = 0.0)
return(mydata) }

That loads the node attributes.  For edges, something like this works:
edgeData (subgraph2, as.vector(edgefile$Gene.1, mode="character"), as.vector(edgefile$Gene.2, mode="character"), attr='Weight') <-edgefile$Weight

If you have multiple edges use:
addGraphToGraph (Cy_Wind, subgraph2)


Hope this helps,

Mark Grimes
University of Montana
